about.intro: Pattes Douces is a community blog where pets, with a little help from their humans, share their adventures, comment and react.
about.body: It started as a student project and remains open: its source code is public and anyone can suggest improvements.
about.sourceLink: See the source code on GitHub

contact.intro: A question, a bug, a remark about accessibility? Write to us by opening an issue on GitHub: we answer within a few days.

privacy.intro: Pattes Douces only collects what the blog needs to work. No ads, no trackers, no third-party cookies.
privacy.account: Username, email address, bio and species. Your password is hashed (bcrypt): nobody, not even us, can read it.
privacy.content: Your articles, images, comments, reactions and the articles you have read. Images are hosted by Vercel Blob.
privacy.browser: Your session and theme choice are kept in your browser’s local storage; your language in a technical cookie (NEXT_LOCALE).
privacy.translation: Articles and comments are translated in your browser by an open-source library (Transformers.js) and translation models hosted on this site: the text never leaves your device and no third-party service is called. On first use, a language model (about 110 MB) is downloaded from this site, then cached by your browser.
privacy.deletion: From your profile, “Delete account” erases your account, your articles and your comments.

accessibility.intro: Pattes Douces is committed to making its website accessible, following the French accessibility framework RGAA version 4.1.2, which matches WCAG 2.2 level AA. This accessibility statement applies to the Pattes Douces website.
accessibility.tests: No full RGAA audit has been carried out yet, so the share of criteria met has not been measured. During the redesign, the following checks were done by hand: keyboard-only navigation, skip link, menus and dialogs (Escape key, focus return), display in Arabic (right-to-left) and in both themes. A full audit (automated tests and the grid of 106 criteria) is under way; its results will be published on this page.
limits: Article images have no text alternative of their own: authors are invited to describe them in the article text.
Content published by members may not follow every rule (structure, language).
Screen reader tests (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack) are still to be carried out.
accessibility.date: This statement was made on 19 October 2026 and updated on 20 October 2026.
accessibility.techHeading: Technologies used to build the site
environment: Google Chrome (version 155) on Linux, with keyboard and mouse.
Planned screen reader tests: NVDA with Firefox, JAWS with Chrome, VoiceOver with Safari (macOS and iOS), TalkBack with Chrome (Android).
tools: Chrome developer tools (accessibility tree, theme and screen size emulation).
axe-core and Lighthouse (automated audit under way).
Contrast ratio calculation for the design system colours.
accessibility.contact: If you cannot access a piece of content or a service, contact us so we can direct you to an accessible alternative or provide the content in another form.
accessibility.remedy: Use this procedure if you have reported to the site manager an accessibility issue that prevents you from accessing content or a service of the site, and you have not received a satisfactory answer. You can:
accessibility.remedyForm: Write to the French Defender of Rights (Défenseur des droits)
accessibility.remedyDelegate: Contact the Defender of Rights' delegate in your region
accessibility.remedyMail: Send a letter by post (free, no stamp needed): Défenseur des droits, Libre réponse 71120, 75342 Paris CEDEX 07, France
accessibility.schemaIntro: Pattes Douces is a community project maintained by a small team. Accessibility is part of every change to the site, according to the following commitments:
schema: Every new feature follows the project's design system and the RGAA requirements from the start.
Every change is checked by automated tests in continuous integration and tested with the keyboard before going live.
A full RGAA audit is carried out at least once a year and after each redesign; this statement is updated after each audit.
User reports are handled first, with an accessible alternative offered until the fix is released.
Contributors are trained in accessibility best practices.
plan: Full RGAA audit of the pages listed above, in both themes and all four languages.
Fixing the issues found and adding automated accessibility tests to continuous integration.
Tests with the NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver and TalkBack screen readers.
Updating this statement with the measured compliance rate.
